How to read it: Very short; this name can vary by tool.
Visual result after clipping: Very close coverage with clear scalp contrast rather than a bare shave.
Common use: A near-skin fade area or a deliberately very short base.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Use your #0 only where we agree on a very close finish; please show me the result before taking it higher.”

How to read it: Between a #0 and #1 on many systems; confirm your comb’s marking.
Visual result after clipping: Still very short, with slightly more visible hair than a close #0 finish.
Common use: A small step in a short fade or blend.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Use your #0.5 as the transition between the close area and the #1; confirm what that guard leaves on this clipper.”

Visual result after clipping: A short, even layer that clearly shows hair without looking long.
Common use: A short sides-and-back baseline or compact buzz length.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Leave a #1 on the area we marked, then show me the first pass before blending higher.”

Visual result after clipping: Short coverage with a little more softness than a #1.
Common use: A bridge between #1 and #2 in a gradual blend.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Use #1.5 only as a bridge from my #1 area into #2; I do not want an abrupt line.”

Visual result after clipping: Short but more visibly covered than #1, with less scalp contrast.
Common use: Short sides or a conservative short overall cut.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Leave a #2 through the side area; keep it visibly short but not as close as a #1.”

Visual result after clipping: A clearly visible short layer with more texture than the lower numbers.
Common use: A classic short buzz length or a higher blend zone.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “I want a #3 in the area we discuss, so the finish stays short but has visible coverage.”

Visual result after clipping: A compact short cut with enough length to read as hair rather than stubble.
Common use: A longer buzz or the upper side area of a short cut.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Keep a #4 where I want a fuller short result; do not take that area down to my lower side number.”

Visual result after clipping: Short coverage with a fuller surface than a #4.
Common use: A longer transition or a short all-over length.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Use #5 for the fuller short section, then connect it smoothly to the shorter area.”

Visual result after clipping: A short, fuller layer that begins to show more movement when hair is dense enough.
Common use: A longer transition or a low-maintenance short cut.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Leave a #6 in the fuller area; I want it short, but not clippered close to the scalp.”

Visual result after clipping: A fuller short finish with a less severe contrast to a longer top.
Common use: A high blend area or a longer short all-over finish.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Use #7 for a soft connection into the longer section, keeping the overall result clearly short.”

Visual result after clipping: The longest common numbered guard in many standard sets, leaving a visibly fuller short layer.
Common use: A longer clipper cut or a conservative starting length before going shorter.
What to say to a barber or stylist: “Start with your #8 so we can see the longest short option first; only go shorter after I check it.”
